cards.text: Ai is a heap of ruins. At that time, Joshua, Israel's leader, builds an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal. Now you might think this was Joshua's own idea. Hold that thought.

cards.question: Why does Joshua build an altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal?

answers.text: It marked the win at Ai

cards.text: Moses, the servant of the LORD, left instructions in the Book of the Law, and Joshua builds it exactly by the Book. He is NOT one of those "I don't need the instructions" guys.

cards.question: The Book of the Law calls for "an altar of ___ stones on which no iron tool has been used."

cards.text: Rocks straight from the ground, no chisel. I respect that, because I've been carved on, and NOBODY asked me first.

cards.question: With the altar of uncut stones built on Mount Ebal, what do the Israelites do on it?

answers.text: Lay their battle lances on it
Pile up the plunder from Ai

cards.text: Then, right there in front of all the Israelites, Joshua starts writing on the stones. Not a doodle. Not a "Joshua was here."

cards.question: What does Joshua write on the stones at Mount Ebal?

answers.text: A copy of the law of Moses
The names of the twelve tribes
A record of the battle at Ai

cards.text: Now picture the crowd. ALL Israel, with their elders, officers and judges, stands on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, facing the Levitical priests who carry it.

cards.question: In the crowd standing around the ark, there are citizens of Israel but no foreigners.

cards.text: Then the crowd splits down the middle. Half stand in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, like an usher at a wedding going, "Bride's side or groom's side?" times a WHOLE nation.

cards.question: Moses had commanded this two-mountain setup earlier. What was it for?

answers.text: To bless the people of Israel

cards.text: Afterward, Joshua takes the words of the law and reads them OUT LOUD to the whole crowd, according to what's written in the Book of the Law.

cards.question: When Joshua reads the law aloud, he reads the blessings and leaves out the curses.

cards.text: Not one word of all Moses commanded gets skipped. Friend, I skipped ONE line on a recipe card once and baked a tray of hockey pucks. Joshua skips NOTHING.

cards.question: Joshua reads every word before the whole assembly of Israel. Who is in that assembly listening?

answers.text: Women and little ones and foreigners too
Only the elders and the priests
Only the men who fought at Ai

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "an altar of ___ stones on which no iron tool has been used.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'Ai is a heap of ruins.' / 'At that time, Joshua... builds an altar...' / 'Now you might think this was Joshua's own idea.' / 'Hold that thought.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It restates the uncut stones the baker just answered on card 4, then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward or set up card 6.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: 'I've been carved on, and NOBODY asked me first' gives Papa Dorin a complaint about the Millers carving his name. In his backstory, the carving is a fond memory, and he asked to keep the name. The joke adds a resentment that isn't in his story and reads like a grudge.

rule.text: Godly character. He never holds a grudge, and his humor reflects kindness and forgiveness.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Not one word of all Moses commanded gets skipped.' / 'Friend, I skipped ONE line on a recipe card once and baked a tray of hockey pucks.' / 'Joshua skips NOTHING.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Earlier cards rule out both wrong answers. Card 9 says ALL Israel is there, card 10 already showed that foreigners are in the crowd, and card 15 says Joshua reads before the whole assembly. That leaves 'Only the elders and the priests' and 'Only the men who fought at Ai' with no real chance, so the answer is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Five of the eight choice cards are multiple choice, against two true or false and one fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. The cards also follow a fixed pattern, alternating story card and choice card all the way through.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
